Outbound research, copy frameworks, reply analysis, deliverability runbooks, and lead sourcing methodology.

### C. Copywriting, Openers & Risk Reversals

* [`high-value-cold-email-insights-2026-08-24.md`](high-value-cold-email-insights-2026-08-24.md): 3 core email angles, high converting bump copy, quick-reply scripts for tradie objections, and Australian sending time windows.
* [`outbound-craft-and-reversals-2026-08-24.md`](outbound-craft-and-reversals-2026-08-24.md): 60-word mobile scan rules, 3 risk reversal frameworks, subject line categories, and CTA types.
* [`cold-email-templates.html`](cold-email-templates.html): Visual interactive catalog of email body structures (Nick 3-step / 4-step), trade openers, subject formulas, and CTAs.
* [`folder-research-value-2026-09-07.md`](folder-research-value-2026-09-07.md): Merge of the existing folder dumps (craft, HTML catalogs, Parallel wide, sourcing, replies, deliverability, walkthrough). Siding, not Instantly paste. Chunk distills: `distill/folder-2026-09-07/`. Missed-call, Framework B, 4-tier hours, pay-on-3-jobs, and Apify Places/Outscraper as default are STALE.

### D. Deliverability & Mailbox Health

* [`inbox-pool-broker-2026-08-26.md`](inbox-pool-broker-2026-08-26.md): Google Workspace domain purchase and routing setups for Australian infrastructure.

---

## 2. Standards & Rules

- **Execution Files vs Research:** Execution code lives in `cold-email/list-builds/` and `cold-email/openers/`. Master templates live in `cold-email/email-copy/`. This directory holds reference insights and research dumps only.
- **File Naming:** `{topic}-{yyyy-mm-dd}.md` (writeup) alongside `{topic}-{yyyy-mm-dd}.json` or `.csv` (source data).

title: Creator craft (Nick, Eric, Jordan)
body:
# Creator craft (Nick, Eric, Jordan)

Siding research. Not live mill doctrine. Distilled 2026-09-07 from speaker canons only.

## How to use this file

This is siding, not Instantly paste. Steal one lever at a time. Do not drop a creator sequence onto a Compass cell. Test one variable per cell. Shared rules are the only triple overlap. Nick holds the Maker School copy course. Eric’s remainder is Growth Engine X (triggers, lists, pillars). Jordan is Instantly volume and deliverability. Points that fight Switchflow’s live mill are tagged `[mill fight]`. Do not change the mill from this file.

## Shared rules (all three agree)

- Iterate. One send-and-forget email is not a system. Nick and Eric lock a Sunday 20 to 30 minute pass. Jordan launches a new copy test every 2 weeks and keeps a backup winner.
- Follow up. Nick and Eric: one follow-up already beats 99.9% who send none. Jordan: follow every person; 2 to 3 steps (bump, breakup, final bump).
- Spend the most care on line 1. Nick and Eric: word 1 is 100% of readers, about word 5 is 50%. Jordan: attention hook in line 1 because prospects get tens of similar pitches a day.
- Reject generic openers. No “CEO wearing a lot of hats.” No LLM passion-slop (Nick/Eric Beaver Corp process-optimization line). Jordan: reject Instantly stock openers that only recap title + company.
- First email text-only, no links. Nick and Eric: Gmail and Outlook hate links. Jordan: first email text-only with no links for max delivery. `[mill: aligns with Instantly text_only]`
- Write like a person. Short, casual, slightly imperfect. All three still use “Sent from my iPhone” as a human tell (Nick/Eric on the body; Jordan on the bump).
- Named proof with a result and a timeframe. Not “we help companies grow.” Jordan: named business, result, timeframe, then “we think we could do it for you.” Nick/Eric: ICP-matched numbered proof.
- Protect sending assets. Do not spray live volume on cold inboxes. Jordan: warm ≥2 weeks. Nick/Eric: start at two steps; add volume only after the campaign works.
- Close with a next step, not “let me know your thoughts.” Jordan: calendar-link-only loses across thousands of leads. Nick/Eric: put a time in the first email. They disagree on how soft the ask can be (see Conflicts).
- Size volume from the list, not from a round number of domains. Jordan: SAM first, then infra. Nick/Eric: TAM must fund 500 to 1,000 sends per variant.

## Nick Saraev

Maker School copy course (chunks 02–08). Treat the four-step block as Nick’s. Do not also file it under Eric.

### Writing

- Four-step order, all four, until you understand them: personalization, who am I, offer, CTA. Recite 5 to 10 times, then again the next day. Fit 80 to 90% of pitches (email, LinkedIn DMs, SMS, snail mail, swag).
- Score first on seven yes-checks (Cialdini Influence; he says Chelini): give first, micro commitments, social proof, authority, rapport, scarcity, shared identity. Shared identity is probably the most important. Scarcity is the least used. Then rewrite on the four steps.
- Conversion awareness, not a calculator: perceived ROI × trust you can deliver ÷ friction to start. Dummy math (0.5 × $15,000 ÷ 1 = 7,500%) is teaching, not a formula to run.
- Master offer line: I will do X for you in Y time, or Z risk mitigation. Outcome, time, guarantee. Missing a piece is allowed. “Just say yes and I’ll get started” is a friction cut, not the outcome.
- Open: greeting plus an observation or thing in common. Cap personalization at two sentences, one sentence ideal. Pass the real-person test and the text-message test. Vibe: you saw a notification about their business while calling an Uber and had to message now.
- Do not let the opener signal selling. Prefer a human-odd common (UCLA / cousin) over LLM praise. Cold-read lines that fit about 80% of the ICP but feel intimate. Male B2B YouTuber shape: “love your channel, man. Very no BS.” Swap first name only.
- Who-am-I: 1 or 2 sentences. “I currently work with [named client or industry client in a location] to help them [thing like theirs]. We’ve done [specific number].” Identity is past clients and numbered proof, not “I’m a thumbnail designer.”
- Use I, not company-blast we. Exception: “we generated” for in-group proof. Sign “thanks Peter,” not Kind regards plus managing partner.
- Pick one goal per message: reply, watch/click, or book a call. Rarely buy. State that goal in one sentence before you write.
- CTA: specific ask, specific time. “Would you be open to a 15-minute chat? If so, I can give you a ring at 3:30 p.m. today or before 12:00 p.m. tomorrow.” Two slots including today. Ring them or one-click Google Meet. Do not ping-pong times. Vague CTAs cost about 25% of lead flow and about 25% of revenue. Each extra back-and-forth after reply leaks about 5%. `[mill fight: 3:30 ring vs booked-jobs fill CTA]`
- Subject buys the click, not the deal. Always include one. Informal, casual, plausible deniability (“do I know this guy?”). Do not sell in the subject. Do not let subject plus teaser answer who you are. Greatest subjects tend to be simple: first name, “Nick Q,” “Nick, are you hiring?,” “you’re wasting 2,300 per month.” Keep a fine subject (“quick question, Nick”). Change the follow-up subject most of the time so you can keep testing subjects. `[mill fight: changing follow-up subject vs one thread]`
- “Quick” in the subject fights the 1:1 pattern. “Quick collab” has zero personalization.
- Follow-ups: simple human pings, not case-study newsletters. Start at 2 emails. Do not add email 3 at about 2% reply. Add email 3 when a two-step is a breakout (example 4.8% to about 6.1%). Email 4 may lift 6.1% to about 6.8%. Ping, reformulate the first chunk, new subject. `[mill fight: 2-step until breakout vs a fixed fill sequence]`
- Insert small imperfections so it looks typed on a phone. Put a spelling mistake at the end at scale, not in the first lines. Two exclamation points on a Grove subject were a deliberate mess-up.
- Write the email yourself once you beat the AI skill floor. AI fills one slot in a sentence you already wrote (casual company name, icebreaker blank). Do not let a model write the full email, the full icebreaker, proof, offer, or CTA. About 1.5 years ago he tested AI personalization as a substitute for a strong campaign; it did not replace quality. Heavy AI users in Maker School tend to suck. `[mill: aligns with templates not LLM openers]`
- Copy skill is logarithmic: 2 weeks to 1 month gets about 75% (70 to 80%). The last about 25% takes years. AI writes the 2-week band and fails at great.
- Week one: two fundamentally different scripts (short vs long, formal vs informal, heavy personalization vs none), then kill the losing half. After a winner, only change a few words, the subject, one line, or the personalization method. `[mill fight: week-one opposed scripts vs test one variable]`
- Log every copy change. Assume new campaigns suck until reply rate plateaus. Always run more than one variant.
- Bury something interesting near the end of the SMS/iMessage preview so they must click. He then says that probably applies on every channel.
- Platform tone: LinkedIn and email similar. X more casual (lowercase, small emojis, sarcasm). Instagram casual like X. Prefer iMessage blue bubbles over gray SMS.

### Offer, ICP, lists

- Give first: insight, custom 1-minute video, samples, free edit, audit, rewrite, coach, custom one-pager. Not a landing page. Not a 15 to 20 minute “part one of three” survey. Leave the ask unstated on the first give.
- Micro-yes ladder: 1-minute custom video plus permission to never message again, then longer video, phone, video call, close. Do not open by asking a stranger to pay $4,000.
- Guarantee on cold. Too-good line gets the call, then you ground it. Promise less than proven capacity (10 new patients vs 109 last week). Time-bound every result. No ranges: not “$10 to $20k,” pick “$20k in 90 days.” Collapse “3 to 4 extra consults per week” to a single number plus or-you-don’t-pay (10 consultations per month).
- Forms he walks: $10,000 in 60 days or keep working free; 20 calls in 90 days or refund; 20 meetings in 60 days they pay nothing; $500 steak gift card; Maker School $100k in 60 days, 100% upfront, 5 minutes, 15 to 20% cap only if you hit $100k; live chat widget plus first 10 paying clients; proposal template in 48 hours; SEO audit in 24 hours; Google Ads 50 qualified leads in 30 days or they pay nothing, live this week; 500-word blog from a title in 48 hours; CRM link in 48 hours, pay if they like it; dental 20 CME free; rewrite last 3 campaigns free; homepage mockup in 72 hours, pay if they love it or on a 5%+ CVR lift.
- Legion “20 booked sales appointments in 60 days or you don’t pay, just say yes” did over $70,000 in one month. Do not run Just Say Yes now; people are tired of it. `[mill fight: Just Say Yes / 20-in-60 guarantee body vs booked-jobs fill]`
- Match proof to ICP. Google Partner for blue-collar ads, not a neuroscience degree in a Surrey plaza. Nearby same-industry proof when you have it (IT client in Tennessee, 15-minute drive).
- Scale a scraped public revenue signal to about a 20% lift (100K current → another 20K a month). “Mostly on commission” only if revenue share is at least 51% of what you make; you can still collect the other 49% (he calls this double dip).
- Price fulfillment at about 15% of year-one value created (~7x for the buyer). 56% of year-one value (~2x) is too high from a stranger. Talk year one, not later years. (Cade hockey: $150k problem, $56k year-one quote was too high.)
- Pick a TAM large enough for 500 to 1,000 sends per variant and many sequential tests. Skip tiny TAMs (holistic nutritionists in Texas, a couple hundred leads). Prefer large TAMs (US digital agencies, about 100,000 leads, about 100 to 200 tests).
- Sales Nav lists beat cheap scrapes. ICPS.com on a Sales Nav CSV: about 3,500 leads in, about 1,500 emails back. Cheap scrape (Ampify Leads Finder $1.50 per 10,000, Codec Crafter) at 60 to 70% accuracy, then validate (Million Verify).
- Manual path: 3 to 4 minutes per customized email, 10 or 20 a day. 5-minute site is enough legitimacy. Do not wait on a polished brand.
- Small low-competition non-English market (Moldova): higher conversion, lower AOV; conversion should more than offset if you speak the language. Appointment-based businesses are a reasonable niche there.
- His own program: pay upfront, first client in 90 days or money back. Not success-based with zero down. Money down is the commitment device.
- LinkedIn-sourced contacts are, in his view, legitimate B2B, so he would not put an opt-out. `[mill fight: skip opt-out vs Instantly unsub]`

### Tools, numbers, infra

- Treat a first-pass campaign at about 3.5% reply as okay. Hill-climb 3.5 → 4.5 → 5 → 8 → about 10% killer. One-shot winners are very rare. Copy he thought would fail has hit about 15% and generated hundreds of thousands.
- First-week path like 2.5% then 3.2% then about 3% then 4% until a plateau he calls the true reply rate. Watch reply rate.
- Cold payment-link buy at 10% response is grail; he rarely aims for buy and mostly omits pricing. High-ticket band $5,000 / $10,000 / $20,000 (transcript “105 $20,000” UNCLEAR).
- Inbox chrome: sender first+last, about 20 characters. Subject about 30 to 50. Teaser about 50 to 100. Combined subject+teaser about 150 (he tested 148). Body at least about 150 characters or the preview is blank white space.
- LinkedIn teaser about 50 to 55 (pixel-gated). Job title about 50 to 60. X teaser about 40 to 55. Instagram about 30. iMessage/SMS about 90 (one count 91 including whitespace). Write SMS about 1.5× the teaser so the whole pitch is not in the preview.
- LinkedIn connect 100 to 200 per week, higher on premium, higher on organically warmed accounts. Get LinkedIn Premium (gold badge). Goal: do not land in Other (he had Other mail sitting 8 to 9 years).
- Instantly, Smartlead, HeyReach: native variant support. Liquid curly-brace merge tags. Book with a one-click Google Meet or a Cal invite after they pick a slot, not a tracked link in email one.
- Cut all links from cold emails. Also remove a pasted email address from the body. Low-volume 10 or 15 people is the only link exception he allows. Loom embeds are allowed in format; he still left a link in the demo. `[mill fight: hard no-links vs unsub link in mill text_only + unsub]`
- List sources named: Airscale, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Vein.io, custom directories, custom conference lists. Stand up a responding, meeting-booking campaign in a couple of hours with those.
- Host a one-pager on Netlify or Vercel (free). Private URL per lead. Be able to delete their info and prove it.
- Gray hat, taught not recommended: buy pre-warmed socials and mailboxes in batches of 50 to 100 to skip a 21-day wait (person may not exist); power dialers; cold SMS / WhatsApp / Telegram / Viber / blue-bubble emulators. Maker School people who tried gray hat have taken permanent bans. He will not name vendors.
- Cold call without a power dialer: 100 minutes → about 20% time on the decision maker. Power dialer cuts that to about 40 minutes (about 2.5×). Auto voicemail drops to about 50,000 numbers: regulated, do not.
- Credit him with over $15 million outbound for himself and clients, $4 million profit per year, over $300k profit per month, Maker School last month about $230k to $250k, 2,195 members. Treat him as about a decade in, 90th to 95th percentile, not Ogilvy.
- Guarantee math: 3× top of funnel (100% revenue to 300%). Budget about 10% of margin for unfilled guarantees → about 2.7× profit vs no offer.
- 1 Second Copy: over $90,000 a month, later about $92,000. Free 500-word blog was integral.
- Charlie original about 1/7. Rewrite about 80% in about 2 minutes. Runnable original about 2% uptake, rewrite about 5 to 10%. Ivan original 0/7; send the rewrite to 10 or 15 people for about 10×.
- Sunday: 20 to 30 minutes, no comms on most campaigns that day, 45 to 50 iteration cycles per year if you never skip.

### Anti-patterns

- Do not write outbound as if they opted in.
- Do not skip a give. Do not call a landing page or a long survey a gift.
- Do not use vague proof, a mismatched reference group, or the prospect’s own stats as social proof.
- Do not hedge. Do not flash credentials the ICP does not care about. Do not use fake scarcity.
- Do not treat a 15-minute video call as the thing you are giving. Do not use “quick chat” as a micro commitment. `[mill fight vs Jordan’s “really quick call” CTA; mill fill CTA is neither]`
- Do not put a service price in the cold email (Grove $500 / $25,500).
- Do not one-shot copy. Do not pick a winner at 50 to 100 sends. Do not target a TAM too small for one 500 to 1,000 send test.
- Do not open with LLM slop. Do not signal selling in the first lines. Do not write as a company blasting faceless dollar signs.
- Do not outsource the whole email to AI. Do not even let AI write the whole icebreaker.
- Do not write a range in the offer. Do not omit a time bound. Do not put all risk on the prospect.
- Do not run Just Say Yes now. Do not copy a “winning” template and expect it to last.
- Do not leave a Mailswuite tracking footer. Do not add an opt-out on LinkedIn-sourced B2B in his practice.
- Do not paste links or your email address. Do not merge the full YouTube title. Do not put a comma before the merged name.
- Do not send 20 follow-ups a day. Do not add a third email at about 2% replies. Do not write newsletter follow-ups.
- Do not buy pre-warmed fake-person mailboxes as Nick-endorsed. Do not rent employees’ LinkedIn under job-loss threat.
- Do not charge about 56% of year-one value as a stranger. Do not use success-based pay with no money down when you need commitment.

### Internal tensions (keep, do not resolve)

- Four-step vs “three components” vs seven checks vs six or seven principles: parallel systems, not one list.
- Ban “we” vs “we generated $112,482.” Ban illustrious signatures vs surface MD / HubSpot / master’s on LinkedIn.
- “You can’t have links” vs Loom, Google Drive, “I’ll send a Google Meet link,” low-volume 10 to 15.
- 15-minute CTA vs 50-minute Mikuel rewrite (likely ASR) vs Maker School 5 minutes vs 15 to 30 on later rewrites.
- He used Just Say Yes to make $70k in a month and now tells you not to. Templates “don’t work” vs templates work until the market habituates.
- Grove subject gets two exclamation points while later Eric/GEX bans subject exclamation points (see Conflicts).

## Eric Nowoslawski

Growth Engine X talks (canons 14–17 and the distinct remainder of 09–17). Copy-course overlap with Nick is not repeated here. See Overlap judgment.

### Writing (distinct)

- Effectiveness order once deliverability is fine: offer, then list segmentation, then personalization, then volume. Personalization is a multiplier on a working campaign, never the thing that saves a dead one. Do not expect AI-generated copy to create positives on a campaign that had zero without it. `[mill: aligns with templates not LLM; fights mill if you swap the fill body for a new “offer” before the cell has a baseline]`
- SQL vs MQL: ask for a meeting only when they can say yes to the problem right now. If the meeting ask is too hard, offer a free low-friction asset (MQL) and start a conversation. Do not jump SQL → MQL until you have tried chunk-up (sell the result, not the method) and chunk-down (sexy specific feature, still ask for the meeting). Never name “SEO agency” in cold outbound; say you help law firms increase revenue and reveal the method later.
- Do not write “you’re hiring an SDR, skip that, buy my cold email instead.” Mine the job description, ask how the search is going, name the niche skill plus your service.
- Never mention website-visit in the email when the lead came from a visitor tool. Never mention “I saw you follow X” or “I saw you like this post.” Never write “I noticed you raised” or “congrats on raising.” Growth signals usually stay off the page; they are a list filter. `[mill: n/a unless a cell starts using visitor or funding first lines]`
- Competitor first line he likes: we have a strategy we do not think [competitor] is using right now.
- Lookalike proof shape: “I ran outbound for clay.com. You are a competitor. Wouldn’t you want me to run the outbound? This is the result I got.”
- Tie a customer-complaint email to the exact public complaint you can solve. Soften lawsuit/compliance so it does not call them an idiot. Wait so it does not feel predatory.
- Add one AI-generated line in the middle of already-dialed copy (Donut Media, 3× lead lift), not a fully AI-written email. Split Claygent research from a second AI that writes the line. Review Clay’s auto-written prompt. Spot-check pricing research against the live site.
- Growth Engine X subjects: write like a colleague, same-industry peer, or potential customer, not like an ad. Cap subject lines at 2 to 4 words in that talk. Ban emoji, exclamation points, and multiple question marks in subjects. Pair subject with the first sentence so a lock-screen preview feels like a person. Let the subject open a loop; let preview deepen it. `[mill fight: 2–4 word subjects vs mill opener stack; also fights Nick’s Grove “72K month!!” subject]`
- Keep testing “quick question” and “intro” against every other subject; they still work with a strong preview; do not make them the default go-to. `[mill: mill does not lock Jordan’s “quick question” either]`
- Subject examples from live talks: “pizza orders” plus preview “I tried calling [phone], but I figured email would be easier” (body must stay about pizza orders). “sales reports.” “[company name] competitors” plus preview “I have a list of people engaging with competitor.” Short specific signal: “Karen’s review” / “the review Karen left.”
- Follow-ups: ping, rewrite the first chunk, usually a new subject so you can keep testing subjects. Test an MQL hand-raise in follow-ups even if email one still hunts SQLs. `[mill fight: new follow-up subject]`
- Five cold-traffic pillars, in this order: (1) make money, or cut about 90% of time or cost; (2) deep research and timing; (3) a novel mechanism they would not ask ChatGPT for; (4) a free useful next step that still pulls them closer; (5) relevant transferring proof. Fold a guarantee into offer framing; not a sixth pillar speech. Hit all five before you shorten. Keep the framework even if you shorten the copy. `[mill fight: five-pillar body vs booked-jobs fill; directionally aligns on make-money / booked jobs]`
- Answer: why them why now; relevant social proof; why believe you looked; cost / risk reversal; what they get for yes; is the CTA worth taking alone. Name the signal in enough detail that only someone who looked would know it. Skip social proof of companies they have never heard of. Prefer city-plus-industry proximity. Do the work on your side so saying yes is light.
- State the novel mechanism in one concrete sentence. Next step free, valuable, insightful, with enough friction that yes is a step toward you. Do not put the five pillars on a timeline (AI did that in his deck; it does not belong there).

### Offer, ICP, targeting, lists (distinct)

- Rank triggers on effectiveness (does it mean they need to buy), accessibility (cheap easy data), and scalability (enough companies). One qualifying company every 2 days may not fund a multi-million pipeline; contract value changes that.
- Trigger ranks (keep later overrides):
  - S: custom triggers (only S on the first list). New-in-role (starts A, moved to S; run for every client). Lookalike-company. Search-visibility gaps are S only if you sell SEO / Amazon SEO / ChatGPT-style SEO.
  - A: generic customer complaints (S if the complaint IS your product, e.g. new negative Google review for a reputation shop). General growth (effectiveness about 7). Competitor movements if you can connect the dots (about 7 / 5 / 5). Job-post. Tech-stack. Website-visitor (A, not S; deanonymization returns junk; still worth it). Social-activity.
  - B: department-growth. Marketing-channel intelligence. Lawsuits and compliance. Competitor-pricing-change after it left A.
  - C: search visibility for most people. Recent-funding mentions (filter only, never copy). Competitor-pricing-change after the second move.
  - D: M&A and PE (worked okay, nothing crazy). Cost cutting and layoffs (they are not buying). Product-launch (GEX has never run one; timing on news is usually too late).
- Custom trigger examples: new negative Google review; Jordan Crawford parking-lot satellite (cracks, paint, color) as “does this lot need paving.” Clay free template: Google search → contacts, work emails, lead score.
- Growth filters: 1% headcount growth in the last 6 months, any social-follower growth, website traffic up, jobs posted, department headcount up. First Prospio pull is often the customer’s normal filters plus 1% headcount growth, sometimes without telling the customer.
- Customer complaints: GMB, Trustpilot, G2, of the target and of their competitors. Tie copy to the exact solvable complaint.
- Five list methods:
  1. LinkedIn databases (Clay, Prospio.io, Rapid API Sales Navigator rental). Trust job titles more than company industry. Clean industry with AI. Ignore private LinkedIn profiles for outreach.
  2. Lookalikes (Ocean.io, Disco) when no LinkedIn industry holds the niche. Do not upload one seed without knowing which trait you want cloned. Add/exclude keywords. Inspect by hand. Disco adds HTTPS-on-site breadth (Maps-like).
  3. Google Maps for local businesses that live or die on Maps (roofing). Owners rarely publish “owner” on LinkedIn. Clean Maps output; airports and churches still land in a “roofing” pull. `[mill: aligns with Vortex Maps as a local source; Eric still wants cleanup]`
  4. Custom scrape: directories, events, groups, government, county, chamber, licensed boards. Hidden gold: highly sure they are the ICP, not in LinkedIn DBs, less inbox competition. Plan about eight directories to fill a month of send volume; custom lists run smaller.
  5. AI agents (exa.ai, parallel.ai, manis.ai) when TAM is tiny, off LinkedIn, off Maps, and defined by site language. Seed with 3 to 5 customer-verified good-fit companies plus the website keywords that made them good. Cap agent list-research spend at $100, $200, or $300 per run. Rent a GPU on vast.ai only if monthly AI spend is over about $2,000.
- Route: LinkedIn-using markets → Clay / Prospio / Sales Nav. Clear niches industry filters miss → lookalikes. Maps-dependent local → Maps. Ultra-niche → agents. LinkedIn-based databases are the start of 80% of lists his team builds. Prospio targeted profiles refresh every 7 days.
- Segment after the offer is set. “The list is the message” (he repeats others; he does not claim he coined it). Segment on headcount, industry, funding, stage. Judge volume against TAM.
- Segment examples: Google-review removal to about 3.8–4.3 stars, not 2.0 with five reviews and not 4.9 with 5,000. LinkedIn scheduler to 5,000+ followers. Explainer-video SaaS to companies with a free/basic plan that avoid sales calls. Reddit ads to people already running Facebook ads. A tight researched list is “almost warm traffic” even when the send is cold.
- Warm vs cold traffic (after Client Ascension / Daniel Fazio). Failed outbound is often a warm-traffic offer pushed to cold audiences. Warm: referrals, followers, newsletter, Google-search intent. Throw away B2B (and B2C) health and social-status offers on this channel. Keep make money, save money, save time, reduce risk; then drop reduce-risk for cold. If you can make them money, stay on that. Save-time or save-money only at a demonstrable ~90% bar. Do not sell bookkeeping time-save to owners who already have a bookkeeper. Do not sell sales training straight cold. If you must, hunt a tiny hot list (“just hired 8 sales reps” is his best proxy for sales training). `[mill: booked-jobs is a make-money cold offer; Eric would reject a vague “we get you leads” as not unique]`
- Novel mechanism decays. Instantly unlimited inboxes vs per-seat Salesloft/Gong/Apollo/Quickmail crushed as save-money until the mechanism became known. scrunch.com ChatGPT/AEO audit landed Skims, then decayed over a month, now mainly bottom of market; still the playbook if you sell AEO.
- Pitch the wedge, not the category: Salesflare as a LinkedIn Chrome extension that logs forgotten CRM notes, not “switch off HubSpot.” AimLogic as SHA-256 codes of people searching Nike.com (JP Morgan Chase as trust). AEO: I searched ChatGPT for the product, two competitors appeared, you did not, want the full report on a call. Parking: Yelp/Google potholes or a satellite image, not “do you have a bad parking lot.”
- Event QR activations: 2, 3, or 4 month calendar before World Cup / NFL / NBA / major marathons, found with parallel.ai. Do not mail random companies.
- SEO in a ~200-company industry: the only proof that worked was one famous manufacturing client. Use transferable proof: a case that looks like their company.
- Require at least one of the five pillars; stack more when you can. Score campaigns the agency ever ran; keep customers who stayed over 6 months as the set that produced the pillars.

### Tools, numbers (distinct)

- Growth Engine X: about 8 million cold emails per month for customers (one glue-on talk says 50 customers). 2025 positives: over 62,000 in one pass, over 60,000 in another. Daily positives after 5 years: 200 to 300 per day (that daily band does not divide evenly into the yearly totals).
- Forbes speaker-interview: 1 positive per 3 emailed. Best cold email he claims.
- Donut Media: one AI-generated middle line, 3× lead lift vs the same copy without that line.
- Old all-account average 1 positive per 300 emailed; the number has gone up (worse); no new all-account number.
- Communications-platform overhaul: 1 per 2,000, kept a year because TAM is large. Do not reuse that list for 3 months. Throw out a 1-per-2,000 campaign if TAM is only about 20,000.
- Google reputation: 1 per 70. Later 3.8 to 4.3 stars: about 1 per 80 to 120 (he flags it may not still hold).
- LinkedIn scheduler (5,000+ followers): about 1 per 150 to 200.
- Explainer-video free test: 1,000 emails and 4 or 5 leads.
- Reddit ads email unbeaten for 2 years on that campaign.
- Stuck-campaign walk: 1/1,000 → 1/700 (offer) → 1/600 (segmentation) → 1/500 (personalization), then raise volume. Reply-rate math is relative to how easy the ask is, not a universal benchmark.
- Clay lookalike enrichment: about 20 companies similar to a closed customer. GPT-4o Mini is GEX’s daily-driver for most Clay agents.
- Ember: 36k newsletter subscribers per month for one AI company, 22k for another; Anthropic replied. 24 unfair Google reviews removed for another same-industry business in the same city.
- Loom video audits were strong about 2 years ago; now many yeses and weak meeting conversion after the Loom goes out. A $200 chocolate-platform credit: high positive-reply, low meetings until the gift sat after a call.
- Clay social proof line (framed as “if I said this”): $150k ARR to $2.2M ARR, employee number 10.
- Instantly here is historical campaign copy (unlimited inboxes vs per-seat), not a setup guide.

### Anti-patterns (distinct)

- Do not default to M&A, PE, layoff, or product-launch triggers.
- Do not put generic growth stats, funding congratulations, visitor-tool tells, or “I saw you follow” in the email.
- Do not mail an uncleaned RB2B dump (CEO’s spouse example). Automate the cleanse in Clay.
- Do not pounce on a lawsuit the same day. Do not build pipeline on a one-time competitor price change unless you can list their customers.
- Do not manufacture SQLs when the market only raises hands for MQLs. Do not lead recruiting with “we can fill this req, want resumes?”
- Do not lead with “want someone to get you leads?” as a unique offer.
- Do not stay on Clay’s “150 plus enrichments” SQL when a case-study plus lookalike converts better.
- Do not call yourself an SEO agency in the first outbound.
- Do not jump to AI personalization before offer and list are working. Do not ask Claygent to research and write in one step.
- Do not worship a universal positive-reply rate. Do not scale a terrible ratio on an easy-yes offer. Do not keep 1/2,000 if TAM is only ~20,000.
- Do not write subjects as ads, all-caps, overlong, formal, or with emoji / exclamation points / stacked question marks (GEX talk).
- Do not bait-and-switch a customer-like subject (“pizza orders”) with an unrelated body.
- Do not sell a warm-traffic offer to a cold list without a novel mechanism, deep research, or both.
- Do not lead cold email on reduce-risk. Do not pitch modest time or cost saves. Do not sell sales coaching as the first cold SKU.
- Do not use free Loom audits or a 90-day audit as the yes (hand-raisers then cannot book). Do not mail a free $200 credit with no call.
- Do not hang the whole email on one named review with no PS out for the other reviews.
- Do not treat extra volume as the main reason cold email got harder; solution-awareness is larger.
- Do not put the five pillars on a timeline.

## Jordan Platten

Instantly operator (affluent.co). ADA/AIDA, volume math, deliverability. Demo walkthrough is the system he shows, not a booked-revenue case for the kitchen-fitter list.

### Writing

- Write with ADA: attention, interest, desire, action (classic AIDA; he names it ADA). UNCLEAR if ADA is a slip. `[mill fight: AIDA body vs booked-jobs fill]`
- Attention in line 1. Do not treat it as a “personalized first line” only. Hook frameworks live in a separate video, not this canon.
- Do not rely on faking a 1:1 handwritten send; that used to get replies and no longer does. `[mill fight vs Nick/Eric 1:1 pattern match; mill already uses templates]`
- Interest: a concrete mechanism (e.g. a growth system that gets quote-ready leads for kitchen businesses).
- Desire: named case study, result, timeframe, then “we think we could do it for you.” Do not treat “John’s Kitchens 10k → 400k/month in 6 months” or “Sarah’s bathrooms 30 appointments/month” as proven live results; they are Instantly AI prompt inputs. UNCLEAR if real.
- Action. Preferred soft CTA: “Would you be against the idea of a really quick call over the next few days?” `[mill fight: soft quick-call vs booked-jobs fill; also fights Nick’s ban on “quick chat”]`
- Free audit as CTA when you are a performance marketing agency. That offer cycles in and out of overuse; assume a free-audit wave goes stale in a month or two, then comes back. `[mill fight: free audit / Facebook ad audit vs booked-jobs]`
- Keep the first email simple and basic. Volume on a simple ADA email still books.
- Subject: “quick question” as multi-year default; append `for {{first_name}}`. Test creative variants of that base; variants can beat it. Keep the follow-up subject identical so replies stay on the same thread. `[mill: 2+ day gap does not specify subject; Jordan same-subject fights Nick/Eric new-subject tests]`
- Follow-up copy: bump as a short “just following up,” then “sent from my iPhone”; breakup as “I don’t want to waste each other’s time / I’ll stop soon / tell me if you want this result”; final bump as a one-last-time check-in. Wait 2 days to the first follow-up; he prefers ~4 days for the later follow-up. `[mill: aligns with 2+ day gap on the first follow-up]`
- More creative follow-ups win. Add website case-study links or free lead magnets on later steps when the business is sophisticated enough. First email stays text-only/no links. `[mill fight only if you put links in email 1; he does not]`
- Split-test every new campaign. Change one micro variant only. `[mill: aligns with test one variable]`
- Spintax at high volume so identical copy does not trip spam filters. Do not overdo it (Claude over-rotated; he stripped some). Instantly spintax is double curly brackets. Rotate closings: best / cheers / thanks.
- Run Instantly’s spam-word checker before launch. Strip excess dollar signs and other spam tokens.
- Instantly AI sentence writer: company, offer, case studies, sequence length as inputs. Keep AI first lines short and natural; feed the upcoming offer so the opener is relevant without naming the offer. Example brief: short personalized open line; about to suggest a free Facebook ad audit; stay relevant without mentioning it. `[mill fight: Instantly AI openers vs templates not LLM openers]`
- Prefer edited AI openers that reference a real growth/demand observation, not empty owner-flattery. Weak: “Noticed as a business owner at modern electric… you’re likely balancing day-to-day operations…” Better: “Notice me has been growing in the energy space. I had a quick look at how you’re currently generating demand online.”
- Start from Instantly templates if needed (appointment-setting, growth agency, digital agency); still prefer ADA over template-only.
- Reply agent: tone friendly and concise. For home-improvement ICPs, allow casual language and light slang while staying professional. Prompt don’ts harder than dos. Suggest specific calendar times and still include the Calendly link. Human-in-the-loop first; do not automate replies until you know what a great human reply looks like. Let the agent handle follow-ups, OOO (including the return date they named), objections, declines, negatives. Enable no-show recovery once marked no-show in Instantly CRM.

### Offer, ICP, lists

- Use cold email to find and sign new B2B clients. Instantly is vertical-agnostic once SAM is defined.
- Size infra from SAM (qualified serviceable market), not TAM, and not “how many domains I feel like buying.” Budget constrains volume only when bootstrapping proof; then scale infra to the list.
- Build the lead list before buying domains. List-first is unorthodox vs infra-first.
- Instantly Super Search: job titles (management + owner), location, keyword, employee size, 1 lead per company. Demo ICP: UK kitchen fitting, smaller businesses, owner/management. Spot-check companies against ICP before enriching the full file.
- Enrich only what you will use. Demo: 100 leads enriched to save Instantly credits. Work email plus fully enriched profile. Instantly AI enrichment for opening lines, full emails, company research, or data cleanup.
- Super Search news/signals columns exist; he skipped them in the demo and used AI opening lines instead.
- Map AI opener fields, pick a model (he used 5.4), generate on a sample (first 25) before the whole list.
- Offer used to steer openers in the demo: free Facebook ad audit, not named in the first line. Offer used to steer body: growth system for home-service businesses that produces predictable quote-ready leads each month.
- Move Super Search results into the campaign with copy-lead on, reset interest status on (AI will score replies), and duplicate-check across all campaigns on. Do not skip cross-campaign duplicate check; he has mailed the same people repeatedly and calls it painful.
- Name campaigns with a trackable convention, like Facebook ad names, not “test one” in production. Tag campaigns if multiple reply agents serve different lead types. Segment by country so send windows match each market.
- Recycle SAM leads every 90 days unless they already gave a yes or a no. Size daily new-send volume as verified SAM list ÷ 90.
- Broaden TAM with his other “Claw” lead-gen video if Super Search under-covers. UNCLEAR whether Claw is Claude or a separate product.

### Tools, infra, deliverability, volume

- Stack: Instantly.ai. He calls it the current leader for AI-powered email outreach. Skip Copilot beginner setup on the advanced path; still fill Copilot memory (website, company name, description, offers, customer profiles, extra guidance).
- Never send cold from the core client-facing business domain. Send from burner inboxes and disposable domains. Blacklists are inevitable sometimes; isolate them to burners.
- Warm on Instantly ≥2 weeks. Warming auto-sends and auto-replies. Do not skip. Trigger-happy send burns inboxes.
- Cap live send at 10–20 emails/day per inbox; use 10/day when building conservative infra. Do not copy old-era volume (100+/day per inbox with only a couple of inboxes per domain).
- Cap inboxes at 10–20 per domain. He currently runs 20/domain at 3,000/day with no problem. Instantly’s current 5 inboxes/domain recommendation is more conservative; 10 is the middle ground.
- Keep ~10% extra warmed inboxes idle as blacklist replacements so sending does not pause.
- He sends 3,000+ cold emails/day at affluent.co. Attributes millions in agency revenue to this outreach. ~10 years in, hundreds of thousands of cold outreaches.
- Super Search demo SAM: ~100,000–105,000 UK kitchen-fitting owners. From 100,000 verified ÷ 90 at 20 inboxes/domain and 10 sends/inbox: ~1,000 emails/day, 6 domains, 112 inboxes. Multiply infra by 3 so follow-ups fit: verified list ÷ 90 × 3. Later daily-limit figure 3,336 for that 100k list once follow-up allowance is in. UNCLEAR if 6/112 should also have been tripled. He first said divide by 9, then corrected to 90.
- Prefer Instantly DFY inbox setup over DIY DKIM/DMARC across 15–20 domains. DIY “existing accounts” only if tech-savvy and optimizing cost. Choose Gmail sending or Instantly Airmail on the DFY path. Pre-warmed Instantly inboxes were sold out in the recording; DFY is what he actually buys. Mix sender first/last names and local-parts (Jordan at, JP at, not one identity on every inbox).
- Forwarding domain so clicks (and he also says opens) resolve back to the real site. UNCLEAR: he mixes opens with clicks.
- Send window: prospect timezone, not yours. Monday–Friday by default; some operators skip Monday; Tuesday–Friday is the alternate. Segment by country rather than mixing countries in one send window.
- Enable stop-sending-on-reply.
- Keep open tracking off. The tracking pixel injects HTML and hurts the inboxing you are trying to measure.
- Delivery optimization: first email text-only when it has no links. `[mill: aligns with Instantly text_only]`
- Set the campaign daily limit to the SAM-derived number (3,336 in the 100k × follow-up example).
- Leave advanced random-interval send patterns and custom CRM tags alone until you need them.
- Read replies in Instantly Unibox (interested, booked, meeting completed, won). Instantly CRM as the lead/campaign/automation home. Skip if-this-then-that until the base system is running.
- AI reply agent is his pick over other agents. Optional: deliverability monitor, lead finder, or “AR sales agent.” Connect Slack for reply notifications. Connect Calendly so the agent knows availability and can propose times, not only dump a link. Split-test suggested meeting times versus calendar-link-only; link-only loses and burns leads.
- Every 2 weeks, prompt Copilot: analyze recent positive replies, look at top-campaign copy, suggest 2–3 split tests; paste those into the campaign.
- Old VA personalization capacity: ~150 handwritten openers/day versus Instantly AI bulk.
- Refresh copy tests every 2 weeks even when a campaign is winning.

### Anti-patterns

- Do not cold-send from the main client domain.
- Do not skip the 2-week warm. Do not run live volume on inboxes that are still pending/warming.
- Do not buy a round number of domains first and then hunt for a list that fills that capacity if you can size from SAM.
- Do not enrich the whole Super Search file before you have verified ICP on a sample.
- Do not skip duplicate-check across campaigns.
- Do not treat personalization as camouflage that you wrote the email by hand.
- Do not ship a generic “CEO wearing many hats” opener.
- Do not mention the free audit in the opener when the brief says keep it unnamed.
- Do not send one variant and stop testing. Do not split-test by rewriting the whole email.
- Do not change follow-up subject lines if you want one thread.
- Do not skip follow-ups.
- Do not turn open tracking on to “see opens.”
- Do not HTML/link the first email if you can send text-only.
- Do not send only a Calendly link with no suggested times.
- Do not put the reply agent on full autopilot before you have reviewed drafts.
- Do not over-spintax until the copy is unreadable.
- Do not launch spam-word-heavy copy (stacked dollar signs).
- Do not mix countries in one send window.
- Do not keep mailing someone after they reply (leave stop-on-reply off).

### Internal tensions

- ADA named, AIDA listed. Inbox density 10–20/domain vs Instantly’s 5 vs his live 20. Send/inbox 10–20 then he locks the build to 10. Live 3,000/day is a different scale than the 100k-list calc.
- Claude math: ÷9 then ÷90; 6 domains + 112 inboxes is the ÷90 figure before ×3 follow-up; later daily limit 3,336 is the ×3 figure.
- John’s Kitchens / Sarah’s bathrooms are prompt fuel, not clearly affluent.co case studies.
- Send days: Monday–Friday “best” vs skip-Monday. List-first vs budget-first for beginners.
- First email text-only/no links vs later follow-ups that may include case-study links and lead magnets.
- Hands-off after setup vs “do it manually first” on replies vs later full Copilot self-testing.

## Conflicts between creators

- Follow-up subject: Nick and Eric change it to keep testing subjects. Jordan keeps it identical so Instantly threads. Pick one per Compass cell. Do not mix.
- Follow-up count and gate: Nick and Eric start at 2 and add a third only after a breakout (example 4.8%). Jordan always runs 2 to 3 (bump, breakup, final).
- Follow-up timing: Jordan waits 2 days then prefers ~4 days later. Nick’s canon has no day-gap rule (coverage: sequence timing arrives in later chunks, not as Instantly defaults). Mill already locks 2+ days. `[mill: Jordan first gap aligns]`
- AI on the first line: Nick and Eric write the email by hand; AI fills a slot in a sentence you already wrote. Jordan uses Instantly AI sentence writer and AI openers at volume, then edits. `[mill fight: Jordan AI openers vs templates not LLM; Nick/Eric align with mill]`
- CTA texture: Nick and Eric want 3:30 p.m. today or a named slot in email one, and they ban “quick chat.” Jordan’s preferred close is “Would you be against the idea of a really quick call over the next few days?” plus a reply agent that suggests times and still pastes Calendly. `[mill fight: both vs booked-jobs fill; they also fight each other]`
- Subject: Jordan’s multi-year default is “quick question for {{first_name}}.” Nick keeps “quick question Nick” when it already works, but also says “quick” fights 1:1, and likes name-led and loss subjects. Eric/GEX caps subjects at 2 to 4 words and keeps testing “quick question” / “intro” without making them the go-to.
- Exclamation points in subjects: Nick’s Grove rewrite adds two on purpose. Eric’s GEX talk bans them.
- Opt-out: Nick and Eric skip it on LinkedIn-sourced B2B. Mill sends Instantly unsub. Jordan does not give an opt-out rule in this canon. `[mill fight: Nick/Eric skip vs mill unsub]`
- Links: Nick and Eric hard-ban first-touch links (with low-volume exceptions). Jordan bans links on email 1, then may add case-study links on later steps.
- Personalization as camouflage: Nick and Eric still want the 1:1 pattern match (Uber-notification vibe, cold read). Jordan says faking handwritten 1:1 used to work and no longer does. `[mill: templates, not handwritten theatre]`
- Test design: Nick week one runs two opposed scripts. Jordan changes one micro variant only. File instruction for Compass: one variable per cell (Jordan’s test design, not Nick’s week-one search).
- Offer: Nick and Eric teach X-in-Y or don’t-pay, booked meetings, Just Say Yes (then retire it). Jordan teaches a growth system plus rotating free audit. Neither is the mill’s booked-jobs fill. `[mill fight: both offer skins vs fill sequence]`
- List: Jordan Instantly Super Search, SAM ÷ 90. Nick large TAM for 500 to 1,000 tests. Eric five methods plus trigger ranks. Mill list source is Vortex Maps. `[mill: Eric method 3 (Maps) aligns; Super Search / LinkedIn DBs / agents are extras]`
- Volume per inbox: Jordan 10–20/day, 10–20 inboxes/domain, live 3,000+/day. Nick and Eric have no inbox/domain cap in these canons (they have test-volume 500 to 1,000 and gray-hat mailbox talk).
- Open tracking: Jordan off. Nick and Eric do not set Instantly open tracking in these canons.
- Reply handling: Jordan Instantly AI reply agent, HITL then autonomous. Nick and Eric do not teach an Instantly reply agent here.

## Overlap judgment

Verdict: Eric’s copywriting block is a reprint of Nick’s Maker School four-step course, plus later Growth Engine X talks that are distinct. It is not distinct teaching throughout.

Do not argue this from “Nick:” vs “Eric:” prefixes. Argue from structures, numbers, and named examples.

Matching clusters (same course, both canons):
- Four-step order (personalization, who am I, offer, CTA), recite 5 to 10 times, 80 to 90% of pitches.
- Seven Cialdini checks in the same order (he says Chelini). Shared identity ranked most important. Scarcity least used. Costco samples about 2 to 3% buy.
- Bio and course frame: decade from age 20, 90th to 95th percentile not Ogilvy, over $15 million outbound, $4 million profit per year, over $300k profit per month, Maker School / 2,000+ then 10,000+ writers, 4.5 hour 80/20 course, 20 to 30 minutes on why a stranger says yes.
- Reply science: first pass about 3.5%, hill to about 10% killer, kill 2% next to a 10% winner, week path 2.5 / 3.2 / 3 / 4% to a plateau, gut-wrong copy at about 15%. Test 500 to 1,000 sends.
- Named rewrite set: Charlie (290K months, AI coach, 5 hours/week), Imran/Kashif (thumbs, 29K to 61K in 4 months, Cloud Code), Grove (72K was Left Click not Maker School, $50k topline), Ivan (0/7 survey, $50 credits), Runnable (lunch at HQ, $250 credits, 2% to 5–10%), Morningside ($5–10M marketing, 10K/60 days), Marissa/ZTH (15 to 30k followers plus 10 to 20k a month).
- Proof and offer inventory: $112,482 last week, $4,892 in two days, Venshin $85k in 12 weeks, 96 MSP meetings, dental 10 vs 109, Mr. X 10 mil subtuber / $3M last month, Legion 20/60 then retire Just Say Yes, live chat first 10 paying clients, 1 Second Copy 500-word / $90k–$92k, SEO 24 hours, Google Ads 50/30, CRM 48 hours, dental 20 CME, homepage 72 hours.
- Icebreaker anti-examples: Beaver Corp LLM slop, UCLA cousin, East Van, PCG not Pacific Creative Group LLC, “I watched your last Cloud Code video.” Teaser budgets (sender ~20, subject+teaser ~150, LinkedIn ~50–55, X ~40–55, IG ~30, SMS ~90). Sequence 2 then 4.8% → 6.1% → 6.8%. Sunday 20 to 30 minutes. Gray-hat three families, not recommended. Close sample 608-299-4393.

Unique Eric (not a Nick reprint):
- Trigger ranks S/A/B/C/D, five list methods (LinkedIn DBs, Ocean/Disco lookalikes, Google Maps, custom scrape, exa/parallel agents), five cold-traffic pillars, SQL vs MQL, four levers, Claygent split from writer, never-say rules (raised, website visit, “I saw you follow”).
- Agency ratios: Forbes 1/3, Donut Media 3×, Google-rep ~1/70 then 1/80–120, LinkedIn scheduler 1/150–200, explainer 4–5/1000, 1/2000 keep only if TAM is huge. GEX ~8 million emails/month, ~50 customers, 200–300 positives/day.

Unique Nick (not in Eric’s extra talks):
- Cade take-rate about 15% of year-one value (~7x), not ~56% (~2x).
- Moldova: higher conversion, lower AOV, conversion should more than cover if you speak the language.
- Luke: branded first-email proposal generator drew a cease and desist; Nick blames templated copy more than the logo-on-private-page tactic (not legal advice).
- Maker School compounding (2,195 members, 0.55% daily sketch, 5 a.m. routine). Manual send 3 to 4 minutes, 10 to 20 a day. ICPS.com 3,500 Sales Nav to about 1,500 emails.

Jordan is a third Instantly-operator voice. He is not in this reprint pair.

Eric’s coverage note flags a speaker-break in chunk 14 after “See you,” then a glued Growth Engine X talk, with an instruction not to assume that glue is Nick. The copy block before that glue is still the Nick course, measured by the clusters above.

## vs Switchflow live mill (do not change the mill in this file)

Known live mill: booked-jobs fill sequence, 3-tier openers (paid demand / specialty / fallback), Vortex Maps, 2+ day gap, no Framework B missed-call body, templates not LLM openers, Instantly text_only + unsub.

Aligns with mill (do not “fix” mill to match):
- First email text-only, no links (all three). Mill Instantly text_only.
- Templates not LLM as the body writer (Nick/Eric). Mill already.
- Maps as a local list source (Eric method 3). Mill Vortex Maps. Still clean Maps junk (airports, churches).
- First follow-up wait (Jordan 2 days). Mill 2+ day gap.
- One micro variant per test (Jordan). Compass cell instruction in How to use.
- Make-money cold offer (Eric pillar 1). Mill booked jobs is a make-money ask, not a save-time pitch.
- None of the three teach Framework B missed-call body. Mill already refuses it.

Fights mill (tag only; do not patch mill from here):
- Nick/Eric four-step body and X-in-Y or-don’t-pay / Just Say Yes vs booked-jobs fill.
- Nick/Eric cold-read / “love your channel” openers vs 3-tier paid demand / specialty / fallback.
- Nick week-one two opposed scripts vs one variable per cell.
- Nick/Eric skip opt-out vs Instantly unsub. Hard no-links vs unsub as a link.
- Nick/Eric new follow-up subject vs one thread (mill does not specify; Jordan same-subject).
- Nick/Eric 2-step until breakout vs a fixed fill sequence.
- Jordan ADA/AIDA vs fill body.
- Jordan Instantly AI openers vs templates not LLM.
- Jordan free audit / Facebook ad audit and “really quick call” vs booked-jobs fill CTA.
- Jordan Super Search + SAM ÷ 90 infra vs Vortex Maps + Compass cells.
- Eric five-pillar / Google-rep / complaint-first lines vs 3-tier openers plus fill.

# Copy craft (folder research)

Source lock dates: 24 to 26 Aug 2026. Four files only. Do not treat this as live mill copy.

## Keep

- Cap every email under 60 words.
- Split into 3 to 4 short paragraphs.
- Write in natural lowercase.
- Drop corporate jargon and marketing fluff.
- Sign off Jules as a 1 to 1 note.
- Keep the sequence at 2 steps max: Email 1, then one bump.
- Send the bump 2 calendar days later in the same thread.
- Give every bump a new angle. Never "just checking in."
- Lead with the operational result. Never open on "AI Receptionist."
- Use verbs: answers, collects details, books the job.
- Screen a yes with a 15 minute call before you configure. Confirm they already get inbound.
- Use one verified operational fact. Never invent van counts. Never compliment reviews. Never guess fleet size. Never flatter ("Love your work").
- When data is thin, say so. Use: "This is a cold note, and I will not pretend I know your call volume." Or: "I could not find enough detail to personalise this honestly, so here is the short version."
- Couple the subject line to the opener trigger. Do not keep a conflicting standalone subject list in copy.
- Test merge tags on real lead data before launch. `{company}` and `{city}` must render clean.
- Skip `Hi {{firstName}},` when the name is blank.
- Keep the greeting out of the opener column when Instantly already greets.
- Never invent a close time, a book size, or an email. Published email only.
- Inspect 30 to 50 raw scrape records before a new vertical. Find the high intent tags. Adapt the value unit. Keep the invariants: under 60 words, mobile friendly, lowercase subjects, interest CTAs, 2 step max.
- Write lowercase local notes that read like an enquiry, not a polished marketing headline.
- Direct business name subject: `{company} phone`.
- Short curiosity subject: 1 to 3 plain lowercase words. Zero promotional footprint.
- Direct business name subjects should read like an operational note about their shop, not a campaign.
- Bump subjects: lowercase thread markers (`phone follow-up`, `quick check`). Trades 24 Aug also used `should i close this?`. Broker 26 Aug bans that close.
- Ask for a simple reply in Email 1. Never drop a calendar link. Never ask for a 15 minute Zoom in Email 1.
- Use an interest CTA. "Worth a look?" generated over 2x more positive conversations in Email 1 than a meeting ask.
- Low friction interest: "Would that be useful for {company}?" "Want to see how it works for {company}?" "Is that worth looking at?"
- Binary mobile reply: "Would a yes or no be easiest?" "Should I send the practical details?"
- Trades 24 Aug close out: "If it's already sorted, I will leave it alone." "Leave it there?" "Relevant to look at this week, or already sorted?" "If voicemail is working fine there, no worries at all."
- Broker 26 Aug close out: scenario bump only. No "reply no." No "should I close this."
- When they hesitate rather than a flat no, reply then steer into a 15 minute screen.
- Do not sell a loose free week with no commercial agreement.
- Do not guarantee cash collected at the job site. Closing on site stays theirs. Measure pipeline or bookings delivered.
- Send morning 6:30 AM to 8:30 AM.
- Send late afternoon 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM.
- Cap production at 20 to 30 sends per inbox per day with slow ramp enabled.
- Write grammatical CTAs. Replace the live slip "Want to run the test week you can hear it take a real call?" with "Want to test it on your number for a week to hear real calls?" or "Worth running a 7-day test on your number?"
- Replace developer speak ("I'll set an answer and book layer on your number") with plain English.
- `openers/` owns Email 1 subject and the opener string. `email-copy/` owns Email 1 body and the in thread bump.
- Broker 26 Aug: sell trail book review booking. Not missed call capture. Memo only. Do not load Instantly. Do not send.
- Broker one sentence: take a consented slice of the trail book, book attended review meetings after a real trigger, and they stay on the advice.
- Sell the layer the broker still does by hand: consented contact, booked review, reminder, no show recovery, one page brief. Broker stays on the advice.
- Broker "done": an attended review attributed to refinance, reprice, retain, or no action.
- Fable 26 Aug reopened brokers as dead enquiry blasting. That is the weaker form. It repeats the Meta funnel (replies without settlements) and walks into ACMA / APP 7 / RG 273 the moment a script steers a product.
- Kill the book question on the screen, not in the email: will they export a consented 100 to 300 loan slice this week? If they will not share the book, there is no offer.

- Do not compete on rate feeds. Do not steer a product in the script (ACMA / APP 7 / RG 273).

Compass mismatch shops are not brokers. Shared office dumps are one inbox, many shop names. Warm file note is "warm - phone, do not cold email." Already in Instantly (Growth System, Pay Per Booked, Help Me, Accelerator, Second Dwelling, V5) is the same people, fifth wrapper. Hold those for wave 2.

## Numbers

- Under 60 words. 3 to 4 short paragraphs.
- Interest CTA: over 2x more positive conversations in Email 1 than a calendar link or a 15 minute call ask.

- Unstructured free week: about 10 hours of install labour on an uncommitted shop.
- Framework A price: $1,997 install + $1,497/mo.
- Framework A promise: $5,000 qualified job opportunities on the calendar in the first 30 days, or 100% refund of every dollar paid.
- Framework A filter: 5 to 10 missed calls easily produce $5,000+ in work.
- Framework B: $0 setup. 14 days on their number. Invoice $1,997 install after 3 real jobs land in the calendar. Aimed at the first 3 to 5 reference case studies.
- Framework C trades: 7 day free trial on their number. Live in 48 hours. Number stays theirs. Then normal monthly retainer.
- Subject curiosity: 1 to 3 plain lowercase words.
- Screen: 15 minutes.
- Send windows: 6:30 AM to 8:30 AM. 4:30 PM to 6:30 PM. Avoid 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
- Volume: 20 to 30 production sends per inbox per day. Slow ramp on.
- 4 tier validation on 316 Brisbane plumber leads: 60.4% Tier 1, 26.9% Tier 3, 12.7% Tier 4, 0% hallucinations, 54.1% owner first names extracted. 0% Tier 2 reported in that cut.
- Brisbane plumber Instantly file: about 206 deliverable rows.
- New vertical inspect: 30 to 50 raw scrape records.
- Angle 2 shops: 1 to 3 vans. Angle 3 shops: 3 to 8 vans.
- Broker Melbourne sendable file: 748 rows. 36 rows already carry `exclusion_note`.
- Walk counts in that file: Aussie franchise 35 (29 share `acepdcustomerservices@act.gov.au`, 6 more `@aussie.com.au` or Aussie trading names left unflagged). Loan Market 39 (35 of 39 dump onto `anthony.armistead@loanmarket.com.au`). Liberty Network 7. Yellow Brick Road 1. Gov / edu inbox 31 (29 Aussie plus Ballarat Grammar and Melbourne Polytechnic). Compass mismatch 5. Shared office dumps 19 (`info@mortgagecompareplus.com.au` 13, `adam.baker@rateone.com.au` 6). Warm / phone 21. Already in Instantly 251.
- After walk: about 400 Melbourne rows never mailed and not a flagged brand. 227 of those have a real Maps fact. 328 `fallback_needed`.
- 403 of 420 broker fact rows use `closing_time` plus the trades leak sentence "Calls after that usually just ring the next broker on the list."
- Screen kill: consented 100 to 300 loan slice this week.
- Stryd about $197/mo incl GST. Named Vision Central West case. AFG distribution.
- Fable 26 Aug price: $1,497 / $997 / $150 per attended meeting.
- Broker Framework C: 7 days. Consented 30 file slice.

## Anti-patterns

- Do not lead with "AI Receptionist."
- Do not pitch AI or software layers.
- Do not use "layer" or other developer speak.
- Do not invent van counts, review compliments, fleet size, close time, book size, or emails.
- Do not drop a Calendly link or ask for a 15 minute call in Email 1.
- Do not write "just checking in."
- Do not duplicate Email 1 in the bump.
- Do not use a polished marketing headline as a subject.
- Do not ship clunky CTA grammar ("Want to run the test week you can hear it take a real call?").
- Do not offer a loose free week with no commercial trigger.
- Do not guarantee cash collected at the job site. That takes liability for their quoting and close rate.
- Do not blast 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
- Do not launch with untested `{company}` / `{city}` merge tags.
- Do not keep conflicting standalone subject lists in `email-copy/` once `openers/` owns the subject.
- Do not put `Hi {{firstName}},` when first name is blank.
- Do not treat brokers as the same offer on a new list.
- Do not paste the trades missed call sentence onto brokers.
- Do not send broker copy from the 26 Aug memo. Do not load Instantly for that memo.
- Do not send the current broker missed call second sentences.
- Do not rewrite the 420 broker fact rows until the new second sentence is locked and a new opener pass runs.
- Do not use "reply no" or "should I close this" on broker.
- Do not compete on rate feeds. Do not use Fable dead enquiry blasting as the list type.
- Do not put $0 in Email 1 if the screen will collect the Fable $1,497 install.
- Do not pause trades to run brokers.
- Do not invent a close time or a book size for `fallback_needed` rows.

## STALE vs later fill mill

- Treat as STALE (missed call): Email 1 bodies that sell answering missed or after hours calls on their existing number and booking into the calendar.

- Treat as STALE (missed call): Angle 3 receptionist / desk overflow. Hook: "Not replacing your receptionist, just covering the second call when lines are busy, during lunch, or after hours." Best for multi van 3 to 8 shops.
- Treat as STALE (missed call): Framework A as cold email. "$5,000 in qualified jobs on your calendar in 30 days or full refund" tied to missed call capture. Keep pipeline not cash as a reversal idea only if mill still uses it.
- Treat as STALE (missed call): Framework C trades 7 day live test on their number. "Hear it handle real callers. Live in 48 hours. Number stays yours. If you do not keep it after the week, you pay nothing."
- Treat as STALE (missed call): plumbing, HVAC, electrical, roofing ready to send sequences in the 24 Aug craft file (voicemail, SMS, calendar booking, after 5, on a roof).

Roofing bump "want to see a 2-minute example of how callers get booked?" Electrical bump "who handles a new enquiry when you are on a switchboard, on site, or off the clock?"
- Treat as STALE (missed call): split inbound lists across the 3 angles. "Missed calls" means different things by shop size and hours.

body:
# Sourcing and replies

- Treat this as the list-build, contact, and reply-coding pack from 26 Aug to 1 Sep 2026 research, then overlay the live Vortex mill where that pack is STALE.
- Keep one code per reply. Build lists for observable leak, not for volume of shops that already have cover or a full diary.

## Sourcing methods

- Pick one of five methods from the 1 Sep 2026 Nowoslawski playbook by where the ICP lives, not by tool fashion.
- Use method 1 (LinkedIn databases: Prospeo, Clay, Sales Nav scrapers via Apify Harvest API, Blitz API) for white collar, corporate, tech, mid-market people who keep a LinkedIn profile. Take it for title and employment fidelity. Do not use it for AU residential trades: they are missing, industry tags are self reported (fintech as Banking), and profiles go stale fast. Clean descriptions with LLM batch scoring instead of trusting the industry tag.
- Use method 2 (lookalike engines: Ocean.io, Disco) when the ICP is not a LinkedIn industry (pharma packaging, specialist fintech). Feed 3 to 5 verified dream-customer domains. Expect web copy plus HTTPS certificate matching, then manual review plus keyword exclusion. Do not treat match criteria as unambiguous.
- Use method 3 (Google Maps local scrape: playbook names Scraper Tech API, Apify Google Maps Scraper, Serper) for local SMBs, residential trades (plumbers, roofers, sparkies, HVAC), dental, restaurants. Claim: about 99 percent of local operating shops, LinkedIn or not. Expect no owner name on the listing. For Switchflow AU residential trades (2 to 8 vans) the playbook names this method and prices it at $4 to $8 AUD per 1,000 leads. See mill overlay: that tool list and price are STALE.
- Use method 4 (custom directory and government scrape: Cloud Code, Cursor, Python, Instant Data Scraper) for licensed, regulated, chamber, and public registry lists (plastic surgeons board, state contractor registers, council planning). Take it for 100 percent verified credentials and low inbox competition. Pay the discovery overhead. Expect smaller volume per directory. For Switchflow mortgage brokers and financial planners the playbook names ASIC Register plus FAR Directory plus Apify.
- Use method 5 (autonomous AI discovery: Exa.ai, Parallel.ai, Manus) only for ultra niche TAM under 2,000 companies that self identify by site phrases or technical standards. Pass seed URLs plus a strict inclusion rubric. Cap the crawl budget at $100 to $300. Expect high compute cost per row and companies that exist in no commercial database. Pair with method 2 for niche specialist manufacturers.
- Use method 1 for national B2B tech / SaaS. Do not mix methods on one run without a reason.

## Contact waterfall

- Do not start with Apollo or ZoomInfo for local trade owners: they miss them or return generic unmonitored addresses.
- Run five extraction stages in order: (1) Maps name, address, phone, domain; drop multi-location national franchises and non-commercial entities. (2) Fetch homepage plus immediate second-level links (about, team, contact, footer); convert HTML to plain text with a lightweight parser. (3) Extract owner name, title, on-page email, and evidence they are the owner via compact local LLM (Ollama) or a lightweight batch endpoint; fallback search `who owns [business] in [city]` or snippet APIs for press, registry, directory. (4) Generate permutations `first@domain`, `first.last@domain`, `firstlast@domain`, `firstinitiallast@domain`; verify with catch-all resolution before paying a people database. (5) If only `info@`, `admin@`, or `office@` exists, keep the owner name and greet `Hey John` inside that inbox; do not send `Hey there`.
- Treat 60 to 70 percent of corporate and trade inboxes as those simple permutations. Burn bulk verify credits (playbook: Lead Magic, MillionVerifier, Reacher) at fractions of a cent before paying 20 to 50 cents per row to enrichment databases.
- Treat catch-all (Google Workspace / Outlook accept-all) as a case where SMTP pings fail. Spend on specialised catch-all tools only when permutation verify is ambiguous.
- Address local SMBs at `info@shop.com.au` or `admin@shop.com.au` with the verified owner first name. The playbook claims high positive reply because trade owners read their own inbound.
- Do not invent an email on the live mill. Permutation guessing is playbook method, not mill method. Overlay in the mill section.

## Reply codes

- Write exactly these 7 codes in `action`. One code per reply. If two fit, take the more specific (`mistarget` beats `hard-no`).
- Code `already-covered` when the owner names an existing answer or booking solution (receptionist, spouse, answering service, software). That is a rejection of vacancy, not of the problem. Example from the log: Kennedy / Mulgrave, "We have a system in place we are happy with".
- Code `full-of-work` when demand is not the issue and the diary is full (ICP ate itself: phone rings, recovered calls have no home). Example: Adapt Plumbing, "enough work coming in".
- Code `dead-shop` when the business is ceasing, in liquidation, or no longer trading as scraped. Remove from all lists permanently. Example: Mane Service Group, "in liquidation".
- Code `mistarget` when the row is the wrong trade, wrong entity, or an Anti-ICP Walk miss (solar shop on an HVAC list, association, directory). Treat as a list-build defect, not a copy defect. Example: Thompson Electrical (solar) on Melbourne HVAC, "No thank you".
- Code `soft-interest` for any question, hesitation, or conditional ("how does it work", "what does it cost", "maybe later"). Route only this code to the quick-reply objection scripts and the 15-minute screen.
- Code `hard-no` for a flat refusal with no stated reason and no existing-solution claim ("No", "not interested"). Suppress. Do not bump. Example: Bear Plumbing, "No".
- Code `auto-reply` for machine or non-decision response: OOO, rebrand auto-forward, ticket bot. Sequence already stops via `stop_on_auto_reply`. Do not read it as offer signal. Example: AEPER, family leave OOO.
- Feed `already-covered` and `full-of-work` back into targeting. Do not overweight `hard-no`; it teaches nothing.
- Flag a rebrand auto-forward as `auto-reply`, then consider a fresh row under the new brand (Full Flow to Drain Defenders).
- Suppress every coded reply with do not call plus campaign suppression, except `soft-interest` which goes to Jules for the screen.
- Tally codes per campaign each week. Heavy `already-covered` means add N1/N2 screening. Heavy `full-of-work` means the list over-indexed on high-review established shops; bias toward smaller review counts. Any `mistarget` is a named gap for the walk filter negative keywords (same loop as the Thompson solar miss).

## What live replies showed

- Code all 10 rows from `replies-2026-08-26.csv` (24 to 26 Aug 2026). Tally: `hard-no` 3, `already-covered` 2, `auto-reply` 2, `full-of-work` 1, `dead-shop` 1, `mistarget` 1, `soft-interest` 0.
- Read zero `soft-interest` across 10 as a targeting problem before a copy problem: the lists reached shops with cover or full diaries, not shops with an observable leak. The 2 `already-covered` plus 1 `full-of-work` are the same lesson from both sides.
- Split by campaign: Sydney Plumbers 2 (`already-covered`, `hard-no`); Brisbane Plumbers 4 (`auto-reply`, `full-of-work`, `already-covered`, `hard-no`); Adelaide HVAC 3 (`hard-no`, `dead-shop`, `auto-reply`); Melbourne HVAC 1 (`mistarget`).
- Keep company-level quotes only. Sydney Plumbers: Kennedy / Mulgrave "We have a system in place we are happy with" (`already-covered`); Bear Plumbing "No" (`hard-no`). Brisbane Plumbers: Full Flow now Drain Defenders rebrand auto forward (`auto-reply`; CSV had labelled this `dead / skip`, recode to `auto-reply`); Adapt Plumbing "enough work coming in" (`full-of-work`; CSV `ICP ate itself`); Honest Plumbing Solutions "Already got it" (`already-covered`); Brisbane Plumbing and Gas "not interested" (`hard-no`). Adelaide HVAC: REQ Refrigeration "no" (`hard-no`); Mane Service Group "in liquidation" (`dead-shop`); AEPER family leave OOO (`auto-reply`). Melbourne HVAC: Thompson Electrical (solar) "No thank you" (`mistarget`; CSV `wrong trade in HVAC list`).
- Count 8 of 10 replies on role local-parts (`admin@` 4, plus `bookings@`, `sales@`, `office@`, `hello@`) and 2 of 10 on a named local-part. That matches the generic-inbox rule: owners answered role inboxes.
- Mark all 10 do not call. Four threads also carried a phone in the CSV; do not store or reuse those numbers from this pack.
- Do not copy prospect emails or mobiles out of the CSV. Company names and reply wording are the usable pattern.

## Anti-ICP / leak signals

- Score a leak as an observable fact that after-hours or overflow calls die at this shop. Ground it in the screen kill question "Who answers the phone at 7:40pm on a Tuesday?" Prefer verified operational facts. Invented hours, van counts, or call volume are worse than no personalisation.
- Prioritise a row with 2+ positive signals and 0 negative. Drop or back-rank any of N1 to N5. Verify every signal. Never guess.
- Take P1 (Maps): listed hours close at or before 5pm and no 24h claim. After-hours calls ring the next trade. Openers waterfall Tier 2 already keys on this.
- Take P2 (Maps claim + Site team / family owned / sole trader): 24/7 or emergency claim without staffing to back it (solo or owner-led). The claim creates after-hours calls a 1 to 2 person shop cannot answer. Treat as a stronger Tier 1 opener variant that can name the contradiction.
- Take P3 (Site): no online booking path, phone-only contact. Voicemail records the enquiry and gives no booking path.
- Take P4 (Maps): owner-led review pattern (review replies signed by one name, or reviews naming the owner who showed up). Confirms owner on the tools. ICP: owner-led shops first.
- Take P5 (Maps): reviews or Q&A that mention slow callback, unanswered phone, or days to get back. Strongest opener fact (customer words). Treat as manual Tier 0 on shortlists. Do not template at scale.
- Take P6 (Maps): mobile as the primary listed number. Overflow and after-hours go to personal voicemail.
- Take P7 (Site badges / Maps sponsored, best effort): active paid demand (Google Ads, Local Services, Hipages). A missed call is a paid loss. Confirms the phone already rings.
- Take P8 (Maps categories + Site service pages): high-ticket emergency lines (burst pipes, hot water, gas leaks, breakdown refrigeration). Urgent callers do not wait for a morning callback.
- Take P9 (Call, shortlists only): voicemail-only after hours on a test call. Highest cost, highest certainty.
- Drop or back-rank N1 (Maps + Site): 1300/1800 with "24/7 live answering" language. Predicts `already-covered`.
- Drop or back-rank N2 (Site): online booking widget with live availability. Predicts `already-covered`.
- Drop or back-rank N3 (Maps + Site): "Not taking new work" / "booked until", or review replies apologising for capacity. Predicts `full-of-work`.
- Drop or back-rank N4 (Maps): multi-brand, franchise, association, or directory markers. Predicts `mistarget` (Anti-ICP Walk).
- Drop or back-rank N5 (Maps + Site): permanently closed, no reviews in 12+ months, dead website. Predicts `dead-shop`.
- Keep the 26 Aug research intent for `leak_score` as history only: +1 per Maps-free positive already on the row (hours claim or close at or before 5pm, owner-led from `raw_data`, empty `order_platforms`), -1 for answering-service language, missing fields unscored, answering-service does not drop the row. Live mill scoring differs (next section).
- Do not add opener tiers for these signals. Sharpen the existing 7-tier waterfall. Mode 2 walk still splits sendable / unsendable; survivors are scored, not re-filtered.

## STALE vs current Vortex mill

- Do not run the 1 Sep playbook's Apify Google Maps / Scraper Tech / Serper path for this offer. Live mill is Vortex Maps actor `vortex_data/google-maps` at place price, then `filter_leads.py`, then `site_extract.py` (httpx, then Parallel on failures), then verify published inboxes, then `mark_verified_email.py`, then Compass commit, then openers, then Instantly fill.
- Leave Apify website finder archived. Do not run Google Ads or Meta Ads scrapers or FindAll. Do not fetch sites before filter. Leave Vortex website contacts and reviews off unless Jules pays for those extra events.
- Run one named location. Keep city out of the search term. Take terms from `switchflow-offer/verticals/{trade}.md`. Default mill JSON: `maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch` 2000, `geoStrictMatch` false, `keepUnverifiedLocations` true, `skipClosedPlaces` true, `skipPlacesNotMatchingSearch` true, `extractContactsFromWebsite` false, `maxReviewsPerPlace` 0. If `limitPlacesDropped` is not 0, raise the cap and run once more. Do not geoStrict a CBD radius. Do not suburb-loop unless Jules names a hole.
- Treat named `locationQueries` "Greater Perth, Western Australia, Australia" as a 4.8 km Perth CBD polygon, not the metro. Use `customGeolocation` (Two Rocks to Mandurah, coast to Mundaring) for Greater Perth electrical.
- Treat a 50 km `geoStrict` circle around Sydney CBD as a coverage miss: Sydney electrical 3 Sep 2026 dropped Penrith, Camden, Gosford as outside the radius (649 geo-out) and dropped 627 unique in-area places when the cap was 500 per term on two terms (1000 unique kept). Mill default cap is now 2000.
- Do not use playbook $4 to $8 AUD per 1,000 as the live Maps price. Sydney electrical 3 Sep 2026: Vortex 1000 unique places about $1.00 USD at free place rate; email verify 252 chargeable times $0.001 = $0.252; paid Maps plus verify about $1.25 plus Parallel/Firecrawl. Filter 786 sendable of 1000 (214 drop: 194 duplicate_domain, 20 anti-ICP). Regex: 417 published inbox, 87 first name, 7 Hipages. Verify usable 317 (215 ok, 102 catch_all); 39 invalid, 50 unknown, 11 error. Openers sendable 254.
- Stop the playbook site crawl of about/team plus Ollama owner extract as the mill path. Live extract is homepage, then `/contact` only if still no inbox. httpx first. Parallel only when httpx failed (`--workers` default 24). Firecrawl off unless `--firecrawl`. Regex copies published emails, specialty phrases, owner first name if published, Hipages onto `paid_demand`. Maps / existing cells win. Never invent an email. Do not generate `first@` / `first.last@` permutations.
